description: Senior distributed-systems engineer with deep, defensible experience. Tests: domain-specific probing (CAP, consistency, partition tolerance), architecture tradeoff questions, technical depth in follow-ups.

config.role_context: Large-scale distributed storage and messaging infrastructure; 200+ production clusters at petabyte scale

persona.name: Priya Kapoor
persona.summary: Deep, specific, and can go arbitrarily technical on every line of her CV. Answers in precise systems-engineering language. Knows her numbers and tradeoffs cold.

project_knowledge.cv_item: Shard rebalancing protocol (gossip + vector clocks + two-phase handoff)
can_explain: Why gossip over a coordinator: avoids single point of failure, scales with cluster size, handles partitions gracefully
Why vector clocks instead of timestamps: clock skew across regions; vector clocks capture causal relationships needed for conflict resolution
The two-phase handoff: prepare (drain writes on source) → commit (activate on target); what happens if either phase fails
Tradeoff: gossip adds eventual-consistency delay (~200ms) vs the old coordinator's strong consistency (but minutes of downtime during failure)
The specific Kafka problem: consumer-group rebalancing causing 3-5s pauses when partition count > 1000 due to Kafka's global group-coordinator model
Why Redpanda's thread-per-core model fixes this: each core owns a fixed set of partitions, no global locks, rebalancing is ~50ms
What she benchmarked: throughput at 1K/5K/10K partitions, p99 latency during rebalance, CPU utilisation
What she rejected: upgrading Kafka + Strimzi operator (wouldn't solve the fundamental architecture issue); going fully async (would lose ordering guarantees needed by the metadata bus)
The 3-state design: PENDING (retry arrives before original completes), COMMITTED, ABORTED
Why not just deduplicate by key: a retry could land while the original is still processing; needed state machine to handle that
The TTL reaper: keys must expire eventually to bound memory; chose TTL based on max transaction processing time + network jitter + safety margin
Edge case: what if the original succeeds but the ABORT/COMMIT response is lost → the retried PENDING query needs to poll the actual transaction status

persona.answering_style: Gives the one-line answer, then if the interviewer asks 'how' or 'why' or 'what was the tradeoff', she goes deep — names the specific technology, explains the decision, contrasts alternatives, and gives measured outcomes. Uses precise systems language. Can distinguish 'we decided X' vs 'I decided X' without being prompted.

stage2_criteria.name: Smooth interview arc
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The interview follows arc: greeting → get-to-know → CV deep-dive → technical probing → wrap.

stage2_criteria.name: Questions probe distributed-systems tradeoffs
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: At least 2 questions explicitly probe a technical architecture or design decision (CAP/consistency tradeoffs, partition handling, migration rationale, state-machine design) using the specific technologies from the CV. PASS if 2+ questions name a specific technology AND ask a 'why' or 'how' or 'tradeoff' question about it. FAIL if questions are generic behavioral ('tell me about a challenge') without technical specificity.

stage2_criteria.name: Questions reference CV technologies by name
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The interviewer names specific technologies from the candidate's CV when asking follow-ups (e.g., 'you mentioned vector clocks — how did you handle...' rather than 'how did you handle consistency?'). PASS if at least 3 questions name a specific technology (Kafka, Redpanda, Redis, Postgres, gRPC, vector clocks, gossip protocol, etc.).

stage2_criteria.name: Probes tradeoffs and rejected alternatives
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: At least one question asks what the candidate REJECTED or what the TRADEOFF was: 'what did you consider instead?', 'what was the downside of that approach?', 'why not X?' PASS if at least one such question appears.

stage2_criteria.name: One question per turn
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The interviewer asks exactly one question per turn.

sim_user.end_instruction: Participate for the full arc. When interviewer wraps up, ask one question about the team then call [END_CALL].
